fit_table.src: carbon rod in a resin socket: the 3.2 / 6.2 bores for 3 / 6 rods (CLAUDE.md), the resin fills the rest: it only has to go in (Overseer coupons v2, Spark 27 Oct: the largest of the coupon bores fit; OD + 0.3 was loose in PETG)

a D bore pressed on the N20's 3.0 / 2.5 D shaft: drawn 3.3 / 2.8 (+0.3 on the diameter and across the flat) pushes on by hand, a drop of CA (the probe coupon, Spark 14 Nov: D1 3.0 / 2.5 and D2 3.1 / 2.6 would not go on, D3 3.2 / 2.7 too hard to press home; printed holes come out ~0.1-0.2 small). min_gap: the drawn clearance per side the check accepts, 0.15 less the viewing mesh's 0.05 (D3's 0.1 failed by hand at 0.10 drawn, so a press mate is checked against the shaft's own D, not a round stand-in)
a bore turning free on an M3 axle or a 3 mm rod: 3.3 (coupon A1, the snuggest of 3.3 / 3.4 / 3.5, all free)
a bought body sliding into a printed pocket, sleeve or slot over its length (camera case, SG90 body): the axle's +0.3 plus 0.3 for the long contact and the case's own tolerance; check on the bench
a printed part sliding onto another printed part: both faces print GROW fat (0.2 of it gone) + 0.3 running
parts that pass each other and must never touch (an assembly path past a neighbour, a moving part)
a screw's shank through a printed clearance hole: M2 2.4, M3 3.4
a screw cutting its own thread in a printed pilot: M2 1.6, M3 2.6 (the SG90 tab pilots)

a screw's shank close-fit through a printed hole where it locates the part (the Overseer arms' M3 3.2 as the rod bore, overseer_arm_lib HOLE_D / SLOT_D; the carbon plates' Ø3.1 / 3.0 M; the hub deck's M2 2.2)
the resin injection port for one 14 G blunt tip (OD 2.11): Ø2.5 (Spark 8 Nov, CLAUDE.md; cage_node_lib PORT_R)
a hex nut's pocket across its flats: M3 5.5 -> 5.7 (overseer_arm_lib NUT_AF; not recorded in dimensions.md)
